nodes.name: Ni foam pretreatment
nodes.procedure: The commercial Ni foam (3 × 3 cm²) substrates were ultrasonically washed with deionized water and ethanol several times to clean the surface impurities, then put them into 6.0 M HCl solution for 5 min to remove the surface oxide layers, and rinsed subsequently with water and ethanol, finally dried in vacuum.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of NiS Nanosheet Array on Ni Foam: The NiS nanosheet arrays were in situ grown on Ni foam through a mild sulfur-modified corrosion method. Typically, the commercial Ni foam (3 × 3 cm²) substrates were ultrasonically washed... finally dried in vacuum.

nodes.name: Sulfur-modified corrosion
nodes.procedure: To prepare the corrosion electrodes, the pretreated Ni foam was immersed in 120 mL of 0.5 M Na₂S solution at 50°C for 3 h. After taking out from the corrosion system, the electrodes were alternately rinsed with deionized water and ethanol for several times, and dried in vacuum before use. The as-obtained electrodes were labeled as NiS.

nodes.name: NiFe LDH electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: The highly dispersed NiFe LDH nanoparticles were electrodeposited onto the surface of NiS nanosheet array to obtain NiFe LDH/NiS Schottky heterostructure. Typically, electrodeposition was performed using a three-electrode configuration, with a NiS electrode, carbon rod and Ag/AgCl electrode as working electrode, counter electrode and reference electrode, respectively. To prepare the electrodeposition electrolyte, 150 μmol Fe(NO₃)₃·9H₂O and 150 μmol Ni(NO₃)₂·6H₂O were added into 50 mL deionized water. The electrodeposition process was then performed fixing deposition potential at -1.0 V versus Ag/AgCl for 5 min. Finally, the as-obtained electrodes were alternately rinsed with deionized water and ethanol for several times, and dried in vacuum before use.

nodes.name: Scaled-up NiFe LDH/NiS electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Scaled up electrodeposition process was carried out in a custom-made electrolyzer (25 cm×15 cm×20 cm) with a large-area NiS electrode as working electrode, and a piece of carbon fiber paper (25×15 cm²) as counter electrode. The electrodeposition electrolyte is consisted of 112.5 mmol Fe(NO₃)₃·9H₂O, 112.5 mmol Ni(NO₃)₂·6H₂O, and 337.5 mmol C₆H₅Na₃O₇ dissolved in 7500 mL deionized water. The scaled-up electrodeposition process was performed by fixing current at -1500 mA for 15 min on each side. The as-obtained electrodes were alternately rinsed with deionized water and ethanol for several times, and dried in vacuum before use.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals uniform nanosheet arrays vertically layered onto Ni foam for NiS. NiFe LDH/NiS maintains sheet-like morphology with rough NiFe LDH layer on NiS nanosheets. Cross-section shows ≈1.5 μm-thick NiS layer and ≈0.5 μm-thick NiFe LDH layer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) image revealed the uniform nanosheet arrays vertically layered onto the open porous skeleton structure of Ni foam (Figure 1c and Figure S4: Supporting Information). Cross-sectional FESEM image and element mapping (Figure 1h and inset in Figure 1d) revealed a ≈1.5-μm-thick NiS layer formed on Ni foam, on the top of which was a ≈0.5-μm-thick NiFe LDH layer.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows highly rippled sheet structure of NiS coupled with highly dispersed NiFe LDH nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image in Figure 1e further showed the highly rippled sheet structure of NiS layer, which was coupled with highly dispersed NiFe LDH nanoparticles.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows NiS nanosheets average thickness ≈5 nm, NiFe LDH nanoparticles 10-15 nm diameter, interplanar spacing 0.50 nm for NiS, lattice fringes 0.256 nm (111 plane of LDHs) and 0.295 nm (101 plane of NiS), visible heterointerface. Post-OER interplanar spacing 0.22 nm corresponds to (104) plane of α-NiOOH phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Vertically distributed sheets in high resolution TEM (HRTEM) image indicated the average thickness of ≈5 nm for these nanosheets (Figure 1f). The HRTEM image in Figure 1g further revealed the strongly coupled heterostructure and visible heterointerface existed between NiS and NiFe LDH. Meanwhile, the lattice fringes of 0.256 and 0.295 nm matched well with the corresponding (111) lattice plane of LDHs and (101) lattice plane of NiS, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman confirms millerite NiS phase at 196-219 and 309-347 cm⁻¹, Ni-O at 486 cm⁻¹, Ni-OH at 460 and 877 cm⁻¹, Fe-O at 327-346 and 680 cm⁻¹. NiFe LDH/NiS shows broadened Ni-S peak and shoulder at 357 cm⁻¹ suggesting pyrite FeS₂ and strong heterostructure interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The formation of Ni-S species in NiS electrode was verified by Raman spectra at 196-219 and 309-347 cm⁻¹ which were assigned to the typical millerite NiS phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS survey confirms co-existence of Ni, Fe, S, O in NiFe LDH/NiS. Ni 2p: NiFe LDH 854.9/872.7 eV (Ni(II)); NiS 856.2/874.0 eV (higher oxidation state); NiFe LDH/NiS shows both. Fe 2p: 711.2/722.2 eV (Fe³⁺). S 2p: NiS S-M 162.9 eV, S-O 168.6 eV; NiFe LDH/NiS S-M shifts to higher binding energy indicating electron injection from NiS to NiFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The wide-scanning XPS spectrum revealed the co-existence of Ni, Fe, S, and O elements on the surface of NiFe LDH/NiS electrode (Figure 2b). The Ni 2p₃/₂ and Ni 2p₁/₂ peaks of NiFe LDH electrodes were located at 854.9 and 872.7 eV... In the S 2p spectrum of NiS, two peaks at 162.9 and 168.6 eV were indexed to the S-M (metal atoms) and S-O, respectively... the peak assigned to S-M in S 2p spectrum of NiFe LDH/NiS electrode shifted to higher binding energies.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV in non-Faradaic region measures double-layer capacitance Cdl to estimate ECSA. NiFe LDH/NiS shows modest Cdl indicating increased surface roughness and intrinsic activity compared to NiS due to high dispersion of NiFe LDH nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The double-layer capacitance (Cdl) was measured to estimate the electrochemical active surface area (ECSA) (Figure S10, Supporting Information), which is a vital parameter related to the accessible active sites. The modest Cdl value of NiFe LDH/NiS revealed the increase in surface roughness and intrinsic activity than NiS.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS Nyquist plots show smallest semicircles for NiFe LDH/NiS indicating better electronic conductivity and faster charge-transfer rate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) was investigated at different potentials to further illustrated the charge-transfer kinetics of OER (Figure 3e,f).

nodes.characterization_summary: Powder XRD patterns show only diffraction peaks of metal Ni, indicating plentiful grain boundaries and disordered domains within NiS and NiFe LDH/NiS materials.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Combined with the Powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns (Figure S2, Supporting Information), that only diffraction peaks of metal Ni were detected

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping of NiFe LDH/NiS cross-section confirms elemental distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Cross-sectional FESEM image and element mapping (Figure 1h and inset in Figure 1d) revealed a ≈1.5-μm-thick NiS layer formed on Ni foam
